title: fix(update): restore Gateway startup after legacy config writeback
body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

The branch is in `openclaw/openclaw`, where maintainers can edit it directly.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where updating an older npm or Git installation could leave the new Gateway unable to start on legacy config. A February Git updater could write its original config after candidate Doctor returned, restoring retired metadata, the old agent roster, and plugin install records.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now applies the existing historical-parent write boundary to early automatic writes and passive plugin-record imports. After that parent finishes, startup admits recognized legacy fields without writing state, validates plugin settings against the prospective merged inventory, and uses the existing import owner before the guarded canonical config write. Existing persisted install records keep precedence, and restored legacy records trigger migration even after a same-build checkpoint.

The final write revalidates canonical records under the plugin lifecycle lease and checks the import receipt under the config lock. Original backups, environment references, includes, malformed records, invalid plugin settings, externally managed config, future config, and source-change guards retain their contracts. No store, schema, config option, or obsolete runtime sidecar is added.

CI also exposed an unrelated main regression from #146275: the TLS renewal caller still passed an array after the lifetime owner changed to variadic handles. A separate one-line repair was verified and carried during integration. The identical correction landed independently in #146412 before this PR merged, so the final Doctor squash excludes that TLS file.

## User Impact

Older updaters can complete their final config write and hand off to a Gateway that performs the supported migration automatically, preserving agent workspaces, plugin settings, provenance, and backups. Ordinary Doctor also completes fully validated deterministic migrations while leaving consent-dependent repairs in their existing flow.

## Evidence

- The original authentic v2026.2.15 run returned updater exit 0 but left Gateway startup failing with exit 78. The corrected full replay returned `ok` in **1,251.663 seconds**. Passive observation proved Doctor preserved the original bytes and the old parent performed its real plugin-record write. Fresh Gateway health, both agents and AGENTS-file reads, canonical plugin inspection, registry/config validation, the exact parent backup, and all six workspace files passed. [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34715470503).
- Published npm **2026.4.29** and **2026.9.4** both returned `ok`, with preservation/config checks and Gateway health/readiness/RPC before standalone Doctor or explicit repair. Installed build-info bytes exactly match the candidate; the same-version 9.4 case replaced the published build and was not a no-op. [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34715574367).
- Seven selected regressions failed on the original source for the intended reasons. Focused migration, admission, source-race, invalid-ledger, and built-runtime custom-plugin tests passed. The complete changed-file gate and fresh independent P0–P2 reviews passed for the Doctor repair. Final export/test cleanup passed 94 selected tests and typed lint without changing data assertions.
- The TLS registration error was reproduced by the baseline core compiler. The one-line repair passed the compiler, eight existing TLS/lifetime tests, the complete changed-file gate, and independent P0–P2 review.

Runtime proofs remain pinned to source `9595bf6b9c54e0578bc33f89a3f271c0c596e301`, tree `ff44cbaa7b529f6a36d7878a5840c85250cac9e3`. The npm carrier is `1e21f6eced4d84325a1d14f1b727ec9daae4f8ef`; candidate tarball SHA-256 is `2277197ecd1b39f8aeaec7090092040f55568100ad491caa393e4c189118ac4b`. Later changes only make an unused diagnostic helper private, correct test fixtures, and repair the separately verified TLS caller; Doctor migration implementation is unchanged. The optional second remote February start was refused before execution by the wrapper's changed-base guard; local same-build/idempotence regressions passed. All task Testboxes are stopped.

Some immutable historical drivers retain unrelated final-step failures: March npm expects retired plugin sidecars, January Git references a removed tracked UI directory, and March's explicit Git channel switch uses its old cached host version. The installed candidates and current-CLI recovery were verified separately; these are not presented as automatic first-hop success.

Integrated head `9496707a6abe1d53e0ec8abf6a9a90dd6ea1272c` passed 88 combined tests, the full 23-file changed gate, and fresh independent P0–P2 review. Its [exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34718720747).

Merged as `4017a1a2f44cdeb350833bbce386ba37755f5dd4`. The final squash contains 22 Doctor files; all 12 reviewed production-file blobs, including the already-landed TLS file, were verified unchanged in the merged tree.
